title: Eliminate stale UI idle CPU loops
summary: Made runtime derivation caches persist for an event generation instead of expiring every 2-5 seconds, partitioned invalidation generations by event kind so agent lease renewals cannot invalidate repository Git state, excluded Codex turn-diff refs from filesystem watches, and narrowed frontend agent events to the agent query. This prevents stale or legacy UI clients from repeatedly launching repository-wide Git derivation while preserving immediate event-driven updates.
userVisibleChange: Leaving EVE open, including with active agents or an older polling UI still in memory, no longer holds the daemon at sustained high CPU.

risks.title: A missed filesystem event can leave a cache entry stale until recovery refresh
risks.mitigation: Watcher errors publish a global invalidation and the existing recovery refresh remains enabled; snapshot indexing also retains a directory signature check.

timeline.title: Profiled the exact branch daemon
timeline.summary: Reproduced sustained idle CPU on PID 88316 and identified fork/wait4 Git work rather than native UI rendering.

timeline.title: Removed time-based derivation expiry
timeline.summary: Made repository, plan, agent, and snapshot caches generation-driven and excluded transient Codex refs.

timeline.title: Scoped agent invalidation
timeline.summary: Partitioned backend generations and frontend query invalidation so lease renewals update only agent state.

timeline.title: Verified idle and adverse traffic
timeline.summary: Ran complete Go/UI verification plus real daemon CPU, memory, request-wave, and child-process benchmarks.

decisions.title: Use event generations as the freshness boundary
decisions.rationale: The filesystem and agent watchers already define when runtime data can change. Wall-clock expiry let read traffic create work without a state change, defeating the event-driven architecture.

decisions.title: Partition generations by event kind
decisions.rationale: Agent lease renewals update agent presence every 30 seconds but do not change repository summaries or snapshot history, so they must not invalidate Git-derived caches.

decisions.title: Ignore Codex turn-diff refs
decisions.rationale: refs/codex/turn-diffs is private high-churn task bookkeeping, not product repository state. Watching it consumed macOS kqueue descriptors and caused irrelevant invalidations.
